content.value_statement: Teams often start implementation without a precise, executable definition of expected behavior. This skill creates focused failing tests for happy paths, edge cases, errors, and applicable concurrency scenarios before implementation begins.
actual_capabilities: Identify behaviors, constraints, and edge cases from a feature description.
Generate framework-appropriate failing tests using Arrange-Act-Assert structure.
Cover happy paths, boundary values, empty inputs, errors, and relevant concurrency behavior.
Suggest unit, integration, contract, and property test categories when they fit the task.
Provide test purpose, run instructions, failure verification steps, and coverage metrics.
limitations: It generates test files and guidance but does not implement the production behavior.
It cannot verify failures without access to the target repository and its test environment.
Framework and dependency choices may require adjustment to match the project.
Generated tests do not replace environment-specific validation or expert review.

use_cases.title: Define a New Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a feature brief into failing tests that make expected behavior and acceptance boundaries explicit before coding.

use_cases.title: Expand Regression Coverage
use_cases.description: Create failing tests for reported defects, including input conditions, error behavior, and boundary cases that should remain protected.

use_cases.title: Plan a Service Contract
use_cases.description: Draft failing unit, integration, or contract tests for APIs and service interactions without connecting tests to production systems.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Behavior Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a small set of failing tests for this behavior: $ARGUMENTS. Use the project framework if known, cover the main success case and one clear failure case, and explain why each test should fail before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Edge Case Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Create comprehensive failing tests for: $ARGUMENTS. Cover empty, null, boundary, special-character, and error inputs where relevant. Use isolated fixtures, descriptive test names, and explain the expected failure for each case.

prompt_templates.title: Service Integration Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Design failing tests for this service behavior: $ARGUMENTS. Separate unit, integration, and contract concerns, mock external dependencies, define meaningful diagnostics, and include only concurrency cases that apply.

prompt_templates.title: Production-Ready Red Phase
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate complete failing test files for: $ARGUMENTS. Follow repository conventions, use isolated fixtures and Arrange-Act-Assert, verify failures are caused by missing behavior, list run commands, report test count and coverage areas, and identify the next green-phase steps.

output_examples.input: Add a password reset request flow that rejects unknown email addresses and rate-limits repeated requests.
output_examples.output: A failing test suite covering a valid request, an unknown address, repeated requests beyond the limit, malformed input, and a stable error response. The output also explains the expected failure and how to run the suite.

output_examples.input: Fix a date-range filter that mishandles the minimum and maximum dates.
output_examples.output: Failing tests for inclusive minimum and maximum dates, an empty range, reversed bounds, timezone-sensitive values, and records exactly on each boundary.

output_examples.input: Define an order service contract for unavailable inventory.
output_examples.output: A contract-focused test plan that expects a clear inventory error, prevents order creation, isolates the inventory dependency, and records the diagnostic needed for the green phase.

best_practices: Describe one observable behavior per test and use names that state the condition and expected result.
Keep fixtures isolated, use meaningful domain data, and avoid production systems or unnecessary external dependencies.
Confirm failures come from missing behavior, then document commands, diagnostics, test count, and coverage areas.
anti_patterns: Writing tests that pass immediately instead of expressing behavior that implementation must satisfy.
Testing private implementation details, combining unrelated responsibilities, or creating complex shared setup.
Using flaky external services, production data, or broad assertions that hide the actual failure.

faq.question: What is the TDD red phase?
faq.answer: It is the step where you write a test for desired behavior and confirm that it fails before implementing the behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill implement the feature?
faq.answer: No. It defines expected behavior with failing tests and prepares guidance for the later green phase.

faq.question: Which testing frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers Jest, Vitest, pytest, JUnit, Go testing, and RSpec patterns. Adjust the result to repository conventions.

faq.question: Can it test edge cases?
faq.answer: Yes. It can consider empty and null values, boundaries, special characters, invalid state transitions, errors, timeouts, and permissions when relevant.

faq.question: Can it run tests against production?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends isolated test data and avoiding production systems and unnecessary external dependencies.

faq.question: What should I provide in the prompt?
faq.answer: Provide the behavior, constraints, relevant interfaces, framework, and success criteria. Mention missing information so the skill can request clarification.
